morgan: FYI hit a pyright/pyrightlang mismatch when using our autogenerated stubs for chat streams

morgan: error says: `ChatStream` is not compatible with `AsyncIterable[OutputChunk]` when passed into helpers

morgan: runtime `async for` works fine, but static checker complains only when used as a parameter type

vince: got a minimal repro? pyright often wants the class to explicitly inherit the protocol type, even if dunder methods are present

morgan: yep minimal gist:```python
from typing import AsyncIterator, AsyncIterable
class ChatStream:
    async def __aiter__(self) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
        async def gen():
            yield "a"
            yield "b"
        return gen()
def consume(x: AsyncIterable[str]):
    async for c in x:
        print(c)
consume(ChatStream())  # pyright error here
```

lee: I think returning a generator from __aiter__ makes pyright unhappy unless the class is annotated as AsyncIterable. Try `class ChatStream(AsyncIterable[str])` in the stub

morgan: that worked in my local workspace. mypy already passed, pyright only

vince: alternative is to declare `__aiter__` as `-> AsyncGenerator[str, None]` in the stub. Pyright's structural checks differ between AsyncIterator/AsyncGenerator/AsyncIterable combos

sasha: both fixes OK, but I'd prefer inheriting AsyncIterable in stubs -> less surprising for users and matches expected API shape

morgan: plan: update autogen to annotate stream classes with `AsyncIterable[...]` base when `__aiter__` exists. also add fallback to `AsyncGenerator` return annotation if generator detected

ci-bot: created PR #2378 (autogen: annotate streams as AsyncIterable) and kicked CI :gear:

lee: can we add a short note in sdk/CHANGELOG under devex explaining the pyright quirk? saves time for folks debugging later

vince: also add a tiny CI job that runs pyright on the generated stubs to catch regressions (matrix: pyright versions 1.1.x and 1.2.x)

morgan: will add both to the PR. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
